summary: The study investigates the deposition of AlxTi1−xOy (ATO) films using plasma-enhanced atomic layer deposition (PEALD). The films are composed of alternating Al2O3 and TiO2 cycles, and the Ti content is controlled by adjusting the number of subcycles. The growth rates of Al2O3 and TiO2 on ATO films are influenced by the surface material, and the refractive index and permittivity of the films are tailored by adjusting the cycle numbers. The results show that the physical properties of the films, such as permittivity, refractive index, and leakage current, can be controlled by varying the Ti content.
evidence: AlxTi1−xOy films were grown by plasma-enhanced atomic layer deposition, using alternating Al2O3 and TiO2 cycles. The Ti content of the films showed a gradual increase as the number of TiO2 subcycles increased. The permittivity and refractive index gradually increased and the breakdown fields of ATO films decreased as the Ti content increased. The film growth is strongly dependent on the surface material in the ALD process; thus, this effect was considered when inducing the film growth rates of Al2O3 and TiO2 on the surface of ATO films.
